primary.version: Dead Island: Definitive Edition on Windows
primary.why: Dead Island released on Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, OS X, Linux, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One, followed by the 2016 Definitive Edition remaster. The Definitive Edition/Collection is remastered with all previously released DLC, so Windows Definitive Edition is the best complete high-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Dead Island: Definitive Edition on Windows with the included DLC package. Use the original Windows build only for launch-era comparison.

entries.title: Dead Island 2
entries.definitive_edition: Dead Island 2 Ultimate Edition on Windows, or Windows base game plus Haus, SoLA, and all current free updates/DLC packs

primary.version: Dead Island 2 Ultimate Edition / latest patched Windows build
primary.why: Dead Island 2 released on Windows, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, Amazon Luna, and macOS. The Ultimate Edition/Patch 6 add Haus, SoLA, Neighborhood Watch, and New Game Plus; Windows remains the highest-fidelity complete route because it carries the current content set with PC graphics and performance control.
primary.how_to_play: Install the Windows version with Ultimate Edition or equivalent DLC ownership, update to the latest patch, then play the campaign, Haus, SoLA, New Game Plus, and Neighborhood Watch. Use current-gen consoles, Luna, or Mac only for platform comparison.

all_releases.fidelity: Native PC release with Ultimate Edition/DLC support and the highest settings/performance ceiling.
all_releases.reason: primary: complete current content route with PC capture flexibility; no platform-exclusive story, mission, or mode elsewhere.

entries.title: Dead Island Epidemic
entries.definitive_edition: None; the game ended before a full final release.

emulation.notes: Server-dependent Windows game; emulation does not restore the official service.

primary.version: Dead Island: Epidemic open-beta Windows client (historical)
primary.why: Dead Island: Epidemic released only on Windows and shut down on October 15, 2015 while the game was still in open beta. Because it was server-dependent, Windows is the only platform to document, but the official route is no longer playable.
primary.how_to_play: There is no normal official way to play today. Preserve screenshots, videos, local client files, and documentation; any private-server or offline reconstruction would need separate verification and should not be treated as the official release.

all_releases.fidelity: Free-to-play online Windows release/open beta; servers closed October 15, 2015.
all_releases.reason: Primary because it is the only shipped platform, though official play is no longer available.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only one platform is sourced. The issue is service shutdown rather than a platform content split.

entries.remaster_caveats: Online free-to-play spin-off, not Dead Island 1/2 or Riptide. It was shut down in open beta.

entries.title: Dead Island Retro Revenge
entries.definitive_edition: No expanded definitive edition; it is included in Dead Island Definitive Collection and also available as a standalone game.

primary.version: Dead Island: Retro Revenge on Windows
primary.why: Retro Revenge is on Windows, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One. It is a separate 16-bit-style side-scrolling spin-off included with the Definitive Collection and also sold standalone. Windows is the highest-fidelity/practical route because the content is the same and PC capture gives the most control.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version standalone or through the Definitive Collection bundle. Capture it as a short spin-off, not as part of the Dead Island or Riptide campaigns.

entries.title: Dead Island Survivors

emulation.emulator: Android emulator only if a surviving build and data can be recovered
emulation.notes: Server dependency may prevent actual play; treat recovered builds as archival artifacts unless verified.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original mobile presentation through Android hardware or emulator.

primary.version: Dead Island: Survivors mobile release (archival Android build)
primary.why: No dedicated entry was found, but contemporary launch coverage and press-release republication say Dead Island: Survivors launched worldwide as a free iOS and Android mobile game in July 2018. The game was server-dependent and shut down in July 2020; Android is the best archival route because APK/XAPK records and emulator capture are more accessible than the delisted iOS build.
primary.how_to_play: There is likely no official working service today. Preserve APK/XAPK metadata, storefront screenshots, trailers, and gameplay footage; only attempt Android/emulator capture if a build and required data can be legally recovered and reaches playable menus.

all_releases.fidelity: Free mobile release; archival APK/XAPK records remain easier to document than iOS after service shutdown.
all_releases.reason: Primary for preservation practicality, even though official server-dependent play is likely unavailable.

all_releases.fidelity: Free iPhone/iPad release reported alongside Android; earlier soft-launch history existed before worldwide release.
all_releases.reason: Skip because it has the same game content and is harder to preserve after delisting/shutdown, with no sourced iOS-exclusive content.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The mobile platforms appear to share the same content. Preservation access, not content, drives the Android primary choice.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mobile slash-and-trap/tower-defense spin-off, not a port of Dead Island or Dead Island 2. It appears to be shut down/delisted, so do not promise normal playability.
